problems.original_statement: Biomarkers and diagnoses are observed when a patient attends care and a clinician orders a test. That visit process depends on latent severity, on prior treatment and often on an impending outcome, so record-based covariate histories are irregular and selectively missing in a way that carries clinical information. Missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history can therefore fail precisely because the recording is itself informative. Standard handling, and last observation carried forward in particular, constructs an artificial history in which a patient's state is asserted to be unchanged over an interval during which the absence of measurement was itself evidence about their state.
problems.correction_note: Estimators that model the observation process jointly with treatment and outcome exist in three separate families, so the entry's implication that the analyst has no principled option was wrong. Two further corrections: inverse-intensity weighting handles conditionally independent visiting when the intensity model is correct and observation positivity holds, and weight instability comes from small conditional observation probabilities and misspecification rather than from marginal visit-rate heterogeneity on its own.
problems.statement: Biomarkers and diagnoses are observed when a patient attends care and a clinician orders a test. That visit process depends on latent severity, on prior treatment and often on an impending outcome, so missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history can fail precisely because the recording is itself informative, last observation carried forward constructs a history in which the absence of measurement was itself evidence, and conditioning on having been observed can induce selection bias. Three estimator families now address this: multiply robust estimation under covariate-driven observation times, calibrated inverse probability weights under irregular visits, and continuous-time weights built from a marked point process. Inverse-intensity weighting handles conditionally independent visiting when the intensity model is correct and observation positivity holds; visiting that depends on a latent state needs further identifying assumptions or a sensitivity analysis. Applied emulations continue to use complete case or last observation carried forward, and enter healthcare use as a baseline confounder rather than as a process.
problems.why_open: The remaining methodological case is the one that matters most in practice: visiting driven by a latent severity the record does not contain, which no observation model can condition on. Weight instability is driven by small conditional observation probabilities and by intensity-model misspecification, and calibration of the intensity model does not validate it, so the diagnostic available does not settle whether the weights are trustworthy. The larger gap is adoption rather than method, and adoption is slow because modeling the visit process multiplies the nuisance components and therefore the positivity requirements, so the more faithful model can be the less identifiable one.
problems.proposed_direction: Adopt the estimators that exist rather than defaulting to complete case or last observation carried forward, and state which assumption the chosen one requires: conditionally independent visiting, or a latent-state model with its own identifying conditions. Model visits as recurrent events or point processes jointly with treatment and outcome, and include healthcare use in the causal diagram as a process so conditioning decisions can be read off the graph. Report the dispersion of the observation weights and the conditional observation probabilities rather than the marginal visit rate, and pair a latent-state analysis with a sensitivity analysis, since calibration of an intensity model is not validation of it.

prior_work.cite: Goldstein BA, Bhavsar NA, Phelan M, Pencina MJ. How and when informative visit processes can bias inference when using electronic health records data for clinical research. J Am Med Inform Assoc 2019
prior_work.what_it_does: Establishes when the visit process biases inference in record-based studies and characterizes the mechanism.

prior_work.cite: Multiply robust estimation of marginal structural models in observational studies subject to covariate-driven observation times. Biometrics 2024
prior_work.what_it_does: Supplies a multiply robust estimator for irregularly spaced, covariate-driven observation times, more flexible and more efficient than the existing doubly weighted alternative.

prior_work.cite: Estimation of marginal structural models under irregular visits and unmeasured confounder: calibrated inverse probability weights. BMC Med Res Methodol 2023
prior_work.what_it_does: Gives calibrated weights for irregular visits in the presence of an unmeasured confounder.

prior_work.cite: Continuous-time causal inference with marked point process weights. Stat Med 2025
prior_work.what_it_does: Builds continuous-time weights from a marked point process because primary-care visit times are irregular and informative and treatment history carries duration and dose.
